# Loop lab — 65–75 second video script

Production notes: use the agreed analytic loop graphic, keep its teaching-model label visible, and record the state being described. Avoid numerical claims until the rendered diagnostics have been checked. The narration below describes the browser demonstration, not a model run.

| Time | Visual | Voiceover |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0–9 s | Title: “OuroWorld · October 8, 2026.” Show the periodic Gaussian scene. | “OuroWorld puts a repeating motion into the 3D scene itself. Here's the detail that makes that useful—and easy to misunderstand.” |
| 9–22 s | Switch to position-only seam matching. Scrub across the boundary; emphasize the position and velocity diagnostics. | “Returning to the same position doesn't guarantee a smooth restart. This point gets back to the right place, but its direction or speed changes at the seam.” |
| 22–36 s | Switch to periodic motion. Change a harmonic, then scrub the cycle. | “Integer-frequency sine and cosine terms all return together. Their derivatives repeat too. But higher harmonics can make the motion much faster. A closed loop can still look wrong.” |
| 36–49 s | Keep the scene periodic. Compare Return orbit with One-way orbit; show the camera-seam readout. | “The camera matters as well. To export a repeating shot, the camera must come back with the scene. A drifting viewpoint can break the rendered loop.” |
| 49–61 s | Show the timeline and seam diagnostics together. | “Check position, velocity and the camera separately. Then watch the actual result. These checks tell you whether a loop closes; they don't tell you whether its motion is believable.” |
| 61–75 s | Export controls, then end card with lab link and paper date. | “This is an analytic teaching scene, not OuroWorld output. Change the settings, export a PNG or GIF, and use the comparison to explain the seam.” |

On-screen links:
- Interactive: https://kavehkamali.github.io/frontier-fieldnotes/loop.html
- Research: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12461v1

End card: “Synthetic Gaussian scene · analytic motion · no model inference.”
